companion_to: MIDI Harmony Analyzer Rule DB v1.8
purpose: Converts harmony-analyzed MIDI notes into chord-relative representations for pattern storage, retrieval, and role-preserving rearrangement onto new chord progressions. This module sits between the Harmony Analysis Engine (upstream) and the MIDI Generation/Export module (downstream), enabling the core PRD workflow: analyze → extract relative pattern → store → retrieve → remap to user-specified chords → output MIDI.

summary: Every note is stored not as an absolute MIDI pitch but as a role within its originating chord context.
The relative representation must be lossless enough to reconstruct the original absolute pitches given the original chord, while being flexible enough to remap onto any target chord.
Rhythm, velocity, duration, and articulation travel with each note as first-class properties, not afterthoughts.
Rearrangement is role-preserving: a note that was the 3rd of Cmaj7 becomes the 3rd of whatever the target chord is.
Simple transposition is a degenerate case of rearrangement, not the default behavior.
The engine must respect the analysis engine's distinction between structural tones and surface tones during rearrangement.
Surface tones (passing, neighbor, approach, ornament) follow their own rearrangement logic that preserves melodic contour and intervallic relationship to surrounding structural tones.
Bass notes receive special handling because bass voice-leading has different rules from upper-voice rearrangement.
The rearrangement engine inherits all hard constraints from the companion harmony analyzer, especially playability, register, and melody protection.
When ambiguity exists in how to remap a note, prefer the option that preserves voice-leading smoothness and avoids forbidden intervals.
Rearrangement must never silently drop notes; if a note cannot be cleanly remapped, flag it for review rather than deleting it.
The system must handle chord quality changes gracefully: remapping from maj7 to m7 requires intelligent degree adjustment, not blind interval copying.

relationship_to_analysis_engine.input_dependency: This module consumes the output_schema of the Harmony Analyzer, specifically: selected_label, structural_chord, surface_extensions, note role tags, sounding_bass, roman_numeral, and partial_voicing_status.
relationship_to_analysis_engine.shared_rules: Hard constraints (hc_*), playability_constraints, and chord_quality_rules from the analysis engine are reused during rearrangement validation.
relationship_to_analysis_engine.no_duplication: This module does not re-specify chord tone definitions, avoid tones, or voicing templates already defined in the analysis engine. It references them by id.

relative_note_representation.description: Schema for representing a single MIDI note in chord-relative terms. This is the atomic unit stored in the Pattern DB.

chord_degree.description: The note's role relative to the chord root. Uses the same degree vocabulary as the analysis engine's chord_quality_rules.

octave_offset.description: How many octaves above or below the chord root's reference octave this note sits. Reference octave is determined by the bass note's octave for bass-role notes, or by the voicing register center for upper-voice notes.

examples.meaning: 3rd in the same octave region as root

note_function.description: The functional role of this note, directly inheriting from the analysis engine's note role tagging. Determines rearrangement priority and method.

voice_assignment.description: Which voice layer this note belongs to.
voice_assignment.rearrangement_note: Bass voice follows bass-specific rearrangement rules. Top voice follows melody-protection rules. Inner voices prioritize minimal motion.

rhythmic_position.description: Position within the bar, independent of absolute tick position.

beat.description: Beat position within the bar (1-based, supports fractional for subdivisions). Example: 1.0 = beat 1, 2.5 = beat 2 and-of.

beat_strength.description: Metric strength at this position, inherited from the meter verification of the analysis engine.

humanize_offset_ticks.description: Original timing deviation from the quantized grid, preserved for humanization restoration during export.

quantized_beats.description: Duration in beats after quantization. Example: 1.0 = quarter note, 0.5 = eighth note.

original_duration_ticks.description: Raw MIDI duration for humanization restoration.

tie_to_next.description: Whether this note ties into the next chord segment.

relative_to_bar_average.description: Velocity relative to the bar's average velocity. 1.0 = average, 1.3 = 30% louder.

contour_context.description: Relationship to immediately preceding and following notes in the same voice. Critical for preserving melodic contour during rearrangement.

interval_from_prev.description: Semitone interval from the previous note in the same voice. Null if first note.

interval_to_next.description: Semitone interval to the next note in the same voice. Null if last note.

conversion_rules.description: Rules for converting an absolute MIDI note + analysis result into a relative note representation.
steps: Receive the note's absolute MIDI pitch, the segment's selected_label and structural_chord from the analysis engine.
Determine the chord root pitch class from the selected_label.
Calculate the note's pitch class interval from the chord root (semitones mod 12).
Map the interval to the appropriate chord_degree using the chord_quality_rules from the analysis engine.
If the note is a chord tone of the structural_chord, assign the matching degree directly.
If the note is a surface_extension identified by the analysis engine, assign the tension degree and set note_function accordingly.

If the note was tagged as passing_tone, neighbor_tone, approach_tone, etc. by the analysis engine, preserve that tag and assign the degree that best describes its chromatic position relative to the chord root.
Calculate octave_offset by comparing the note's octave to the chord root's reference octave.
Preserve all rhythmic, velocity, and duration information from the original MIDI event.
Compute contour_context by examining adjacent notes in the same voice.

ambiguity_handling.enharmonic: Use the analysis engine's enharmonic_interpretation_rules to determine the correct degree spelling. For example, in a dom7 context, pitch class 10 above root is b7, not #6.
ambiguity_handling.multi_function: If a note could be interpreted as two different degrees (e.g., #9 vs b3 on a dominant chord), prefer the interpretation that matches the analysis engine's structural vs surface classification for that note.
ambiguity_handling.cross_segment: Notes that tie across chord boundaries get the degree of their onset chord, with tie_to_next = true.

pattern_schema.description: Schema for a stored pattern unit. A pattern is a collection of relative notes grouped by phrase or measure, ready for retrieval and rearrangement.

pattern_unit.source_midi_id: string (reference to original MIDI file in DB)

source_segment_range.description: Which bars of the original MIDI this pattern was extracted from.

originating_chord_sequence.description: The chord progression this pattern was originally played over, as analyzed by the harmony engine.

items.chord_quality_ref: string (e.g., 'cq_m7', referencing analysis engine chord_quality_rules id)

notes.description: All notes in this pattern, in onset-time order, each in relative representation.

voicing_style.primary_template: string_or_null (references voicing_templates id from analysis engine, e.g., 'vt_shell_root')

structural_summary.description: High-level description of the pattern's harmonic movement, useful for retrieval matching.
structural_summary.chord_tone_density: number (ratio of chord tones to total notes)
structural_summary.tension_density: number (ratio of tension tones to total notes)
structural_summary.surface_tone_density: number (ratio of surface/ornamental tones to total notes)
structural_summary.top_voice_contour: string (ascending | descending | arc | wave | static | stepwise)

rearrangement_engine.description: Rules and procedures for taking a stored relative pattern and mapping it onto a new chord progression specified by the user.
rearrangement_philosophy: Rearrangement is not transposition. Each note's chord_degree and note_function determine how it maps to the new chord.
A 3rd in a major chord maps to the 3rd of the target chord, regardless of whether the target chord is major or minor — the target chord's quality defines what '3rd' means.
When the source and target chord qualities differ, intelligent degree translation is required.
The contour and rhythm of the pattern are preserved as closely as possible; only pitch content changes.
Register placement is guided by the target chord's context and the playability constraints from the analysis engine.
Voice-leading between adjacent chords in the target progression should be smooth, following the progression_resolution_rules from the analysis engine.
The rearrangement engine must validate every remapped note against the target chord's avoid_tones and the hard_constraints from the analysis engine.

steps.name: parse_target_chord_progression
steps.description: Parse the user's input chord progression into a structured sequence of chord objects.
details: Accept chord symbols (e.g., 'Dm7 - G7 - Cmaj7'), roman numerals (e.g., 'ii7 - V7 - Imaj7'), or hybrid notation.
For each chord, resolve: root pitch class, chord quality, extensions/tensions, bass note (if slash chord), duration in beats.
Look up the matching chord_quality_rules entry from the analysis engine.
If the user specifies a key, resolve roman numerals to absolute chord names.

steps.name: align_pattern_to_target_progression
steps.description: Map the pattern's originating_chord_sequence to the target chord progression.
details: If the pattern has N chords and the target has M chords, handle alignment:
N < M: the pattern must be extended or repeated. Use phrase_boundary metadata to find natural loop/extension points.
N > M: the pattern must be truncated. Prefer cutting at phrase boundaries.
For each chord slot, pair (source_chord, target_chord) for note-by-note rearrangement.
Handle duration differences: if source chord lasts 4 beats but target chord lasts 2 beats, compress the pattern's rhythm proportionally or truncate at a musically sensible point.

steps.name: degree_translation
steps.description: For each note in the pattern, translate its chord_degree from the source chord context to the target chord context.

rules.description: Structural tones (root, chord_tone, guide_tone, bass_anchor) map directly to the same degree in the target chord.
When source and target chord qualities differ, the degree itself may need adaptation.
Major 3rd becomes minor 3rd; major 7th becomes minor 7th.
Minor 3rd becomes major 3rd; b7 stays as b7.
The 3rd role maps to sus4; b7 stays.

rules.fallback: If no specific adaptation rule exists, map the degree literally and then validate against the target chord's avoid_tones.

rules.description: Tension tones (9, #11, 13, b9, #9, b13) map by degree name when the target chord supports them. If the target chord's available_tensions does not include the source tension, apply tension_fallback_rules.

tension_fallback_rules.target_lacks_9: Replace with nearest available chord tone or approved tension. Prefer 1 (octave above) or keep 9 if target style permits.

tension_fallback_rules.target_lacks_sharp11: Replace with 5 or 11 depending on target chord quality and avoid_tones.

tension_fallback_rules.target_lacks_13: Replace with 5 or nearest approved tension.

tension_fallback_rules.target_lacks_b9: Replace with 1 or 9 depending on target quality.

tension_fallback_rules.target_lacks_sharp9: Replace with b3 or 3 depending on target quality.

rules.description: Surface tones (passing, neighbor, approach, ornament, arpeggio traversal) are remapped by preserving their intervallic relationship to the surrounding structural tones rather than by direct degree mapping.

A passing tone fills a gap between two structural tones. After remapping the structural tones, place the passing tone chromatically or diatonically between them, preserving the original step type (chromatic vs diatonic).
rules.method: Calculate the interval between the two remapped structural tones. If the original passing tone was chromatic (semitone step), insert a chromatic passing tone. If diatonic (whole step), insert a scale-appropriate passing tone based on the target chord's parent scale.

rules.description: A neighbor tone sits a step above or below a structural tone and returns. Preserve the direction (upper/lower) and step size (half/whole) relative to the remapped structural tone.
rules.method: Identify which structural tone it decorates. Remap the structural tone first. Apply the same neighbor direction and step type to the new position.

rules.description: An approach tone leads into a structural tone by step or half-step. Preserve the approach direction and distance.
rules.method: Remap the target structural tone first. Place the approach tone at the same intervallic distance below or above the new target.

rules.description: Ornamental tones (grace notes, turns, trills) preserve their intervallic relationship to the principal note.
rules.method: Remap the principal note. Apply the same ornamental interval pattern.

rules.description: Arpeggio traversal notes map to the target chord's available tones in the same ascending/descending order, preserving the contour shape.
rules.method: Identify the arpeggio's degree sequence (e.g., 1-3-5-7). Map each degree to the target chord. If a degree doesn't exist in the target (e.g., 7 on a triad), substitute with the nearest available tone while preserving ascending/descending direction.

steps.name: octave_and_register_placement
steps.description: Determine the absolute octave for each remapped note.

rules.description: Start by applying the same octave_offset from the relative representation to the target chord root's reference octave.

After initial placement, verify that every note falls within the playability_constraints from the analysis engine. If a note falls outside the allowed register, shift by octave in the direction that keeps it closest to the original octave_offset intent.

Bass notes (voice_assignment = 'bass') must stay within the bass register. If the target chord root is significantly higher or lower than the source chord root, adjust the bass octave to keep it in a musically sensible bass range.

Top voice notes should stay within the preferred top-note range. If melody is present, the top voice must not exceed the melody pitch on strong beats (inheriting mar_avoid_minor9_clash from the analysis engine).
After all notes are placed, verify that voices do not cross inappropriately. Bass must be below left_hand_inner; left_hand_inner must not exceed right_hand_inner; top_voice must remain on top.
rules.exception: Brief voice crossings in fast arpeggio contexts are tolerated.

rules.description: When the source chord root and target chord root differ by a large interval (e.g., tritone or more), verify that the overall register shift doesn't create an unnatural sound. If the entire pattern shifts up by a 5th or more, consider shifting some voices down an octave to maintain comfortable register balance.

steps.name: voice_leading_optimization
steps.description: Optimize voice leading between adjacent chords in the target progression.

rules.description: If a note's remapped pitch is the same as a note in the previous chord's remapping, prefer holding that common tone in the same voice.
Guide tones (3rd and 7th) should follow the progression_resolution_rules from the analysis engine. For example, in a ii-V-I, the b7 of ii resolves down to the 3rd of V.
Among all valid remappings, prefer the one that minimizes total semitone motion across all voices.
rules.exception: Bass movement follows harmonic rhythm, not minimal motion — bass typically moves to the chord root or specified bass note.

rules.description: In styles that care about classical voice-leading (ballad, orchestral), penalize parallel perfect fifths and octaves between outer voices.
The top voice should move by step or common tone when possible, inheriting sc_stepwise_top_note from the analysis engine.

When the pattern has an active bass line (bass_movement_type != 'static'), preserve the bass contour shape while adapting to the new chord roots. A walking bass pattern should continue walking; a pedal tone should continue sustaining.

bass_movement_preservation.static: Place bass on target root (or specified slash bass) and sustain.
bass_movement_preservation.root_motion: Bass moves to each new chord root.
bass_movement_preservation.walking: Preserve the original step-pattern (up/down/chromatic) relative to each target chord root. Use the target chord's parent scale for diatonic walk-ups.
bass_movement_preservation.pedal: Maintain the original pedal pitch if harmonically compatible, or transpose to the key-appropriate pedal.
bass_movement_preservation.line_cliche: Preserve the chromatic or stepwise descent/ascent pattern, adjusting starting pitch to the new chord.

steps.name: validation_and_conflict_resolution
steps.description: Check every remapped note against hard constraints and resolve conflicts.

checks.description: If a remapped note lands on an avoid_tone of the target chord, apply correction.
correction_strategies: If the note is a structural tone that became an avoid tone due to quality change, move it by semitone to the nearest non-avoided degree. Example: natural 11 on a maj7 target → shift to #11 if style allows, or to 3 if not.
If the note is a surface tone, adjust its chromatic position to avoid the forbidden pitch while preserving contour direction.
Log the conflict and original intended degree for debugging.

checks.description: Run all hard_constraints from the analysis engine against the remapped voicing.
checks_applied: hc_unplayable_span: verify hand span doesn't exceed limits.
hc_low_register_mud_cluster: verify no dense clusters below MIDI 48.
hc_melody_minor9_strong_beat: if melody is present, verify no harsh clash.
hc_outside_chord_without_context: verify all non-chord tones are explainable.

checks.description: Verify the overall register spread is reasonable. A pattern that originally spanned C3-C5 should not end up spanning C1-C3 after rearrangement.
checks.correction: If the total register shift exceeds tolerance, redistribute octaves to bring the pattern closer to the original register range.

checks.description: Every note in the source pattern must have a corresponding note in the output. If a note cannot be cleanly remapped, flag it with a warning rather than silently dropping it.

suggested_alternatives: array of possible pitches with scores

checks.description: After rearrangement, verify that the target chord's essential tones (priority_tones from chord_quality_rules) are represented. If the rearranged pattern is missing a guide tone, flag it as a warning.

steps.name: humanization_and_export_preparation
steps.description: Restore human-feel timing and prepare for MIDI export.

rules.description: Re-apply the humanize_offset_ticks to each note's quantized position to restore the original performer's micro-timing feel.
The relative velocity profile (relative_to_bar_average and accent_type) should be applied to the output, scaled to the user's desired velocity range.
If the target tempo differs from the source tempo, note durations are automatically adjusted by the tempo ratio. The quantized_beats values remain the same; only the tick/ms conversion changes.
rules.note: If the user requests a different articulation (more legato or staccato), apply a global duration multiplier.

rules.description: Convert all relative representations back to absolute MIDI events.
output_fields_per_note: voice_assignment (for track routing if multi-track output)

user_control_parameters.description: Parameters the user can adjust to influence rearrangement behavior.

parameters.name: tension_level
parameters.effect: Controls which tension tones are allowed in the output. 'conservative' limits to chord tones + basic 9ths; 'dense' allows all available tensions per chord quality.

parameters.name: voicing_style_override
parameters.effect: If set, forces rearranged voicings to conform to this template. If null, preserves the original pattern's voicing style.

parameters.name: bass_behavior
parameters.effect: 'root_only' forces bass to chord roots. 'preserve_pattern' keeps the original bass movement type. 'walking' generates a walking bass. 'pedal' sustains a pedal tone.

parameters.name: register_center_midi
parameters.effect: If set, shifts the overall register center of the output to this MIDI note. Useful for placing the pattern in a specific octave range.

parameters.name: humanize_amount
parameters.effect: How much of the original micro-timing to restore. 0.0 = fully quantized; 1.0 = original timing.

parameters.name: velocity_range
parameters.effect: The output velocity range. The relative velocity profile is scaled to fit within this range.

parameters.name: contour_preservation_strength
parameters.effect: How strictly to preserve the original melodic contour. 1.0 = exact contour; lower values allow more freedom for voice-leading optimization.

parameters.name: avoid_tone_strictness
parameters.effect: 'strict' enforces all avoid tones from chord_quality_rules. 'permissive' allows passing avoid tones on weak beats. 'style_dependent' follows the analysis engine's style_tension_preferences.

special_rearrangement_cases.description: Edge cases that require specific handling beyond the standard pipeline.

cases.description: Simplest case: same chord quality, different root (e.g., Cmaj7 → Ebmaj7). Pure degree mapping with transposition-like behavior, but still using degree mapping rather than interval transposition.
cases.method: Direct degree-to-degree mapping. Octave placement follows register rules.

cases.description: When source and target share common tones (e.g., Cmaj7 → Am7 share C, E, G), prefer holding common tones in the same voice.
cases.method: Identify common pitch classes between source and target chord tones. Assign common tones first, then remap remaining notes.

cases.description: When the target chord is a tritone sub of a dominant chord in the source, guide tones (3 and b7) swap roles but maintain pitch proximity.
cases.method: The 3rd of the source becomes the b7 of the tritone sub, and vice versa. Other tones follow standard degree mapping.

mapping.F (b7 of G7): F (3rd of Db7) — common tone hold

cases.description: When the target is a slash chord (e.g., Cmaj7/E), the bass note is specified independently of the root.
cases.method: Map the bass voice to the specified slash bass note. Map upper voices normally using the root-based degree system. Verify no mud in low register between bass and lower inner voices.

cases.description: Target chord has more extensions than source (e.g., source was Dm, target is Dm11).
cases.method: Map existing notes by degree. If the target has additional available tensions not present in the source, do NOT auto-add them. The rearrangement engine preserves the source pattern's density. Users can request enrichment separately.

cases.description: Target chord has fewer extensions than source (e.g., source was Cmaj9, target is C).
cases.method: Notes whose degrees don't exist in the simpler target (e.g., 9th, 7th) follow the tension_fallback_rules. Typically replaced with the nearest available chord tone.

cases.description: The selected pattern has more chord changes than the user's target progression.
cases.method: Truncate at the nearest phrase boundary. If no clean boundary exists, truncate at the last complete bar. Log the truncation for user review.

cases.description: The user's target progression is longer than the selected pattern.
cases.method: Options: (1) loop the pattern, (2) extend by repeating the last phrase with variation, (3) fill remaining bars with a complementary pattern from the DB. Default: loop with a flag suggesting the user review the loop point.

cases.description: Source pattern is in 4/4 but target requires 3/4 (or vice versa).
cases.method: This is a complex transformation. For MVP, flag as incompatible and suggest the user select a pattern in the matching meter. For future versions, implement rhythmic re-gridding that preserves the rhythmic profile's character.

retrieval_matching_rules.description: Rules for finding the best pattern in the DB to match a user's request. This is the 'Retrieval' part of the PRD's Phase 3.

matching_dimensions.description: How well the source pattern's chord sequence quality types match the target. A pattern originally on ii-V-I is a better match for a target ii-V-I than a pattern from IV-V-I.
Match on dominant_subdivision, syncopation_level, and pattern_type.
Pattern style matches the user's requested style.
Pattern voicing characteristics match user preference.
Pattern energy trajectory matches desired feel.
Pattern length matches or is easily adaptable to target length.
Pattern register range is compatible with target instrument and desired register.

retrieval_workflow: Parse user request: chord progression, style, density preference, length, etc.
Filter patterns by hard requirements: meter match, minimum length, instrument role.
Score remaining patterns on each matching_dimension.
Return top N candidates ranked by weighted total score.
For each candidate, preview the rearrangement result by running the rearrangement pipeline in preview mode (fast, no humanization).
Present previews to user for selection.

output_schema.description: The output of the rearrangement engine: a complete set of absolute MIDI events ready for export.

metadata.tpqn: integer (ticks per quarter note for MIDI export)

developer_notes: This module is designed to work in tandem with the Harmony Analyzer Rule DB v1.8. Do not duplicate rules already specified there.
The degree_translation rules cover the most common chord quality changes. Extend the quality_change_adaptation table as new chord types are encountered.
The tension_fallback_rules are conservative by default. For jazz contexts, consider allowing more tension preservation even when the target chord quality differs.

Voice-leading optimization (step 5) is the most computationally expensive part. For MVP, a greedy nearest-pitch approach is sufficient. For production, consider a global optimization that minimizes total voice motion across the entire progression.
The retrieval_matching_rules should be tuned empirically as the Pattern DB grows. Initial weights are estimates.
The contour_context fields are critical for natural-sounding surface tone rearrangement. Invest in accurate contour extraction during the conversion step.
For MVP, focus on single-instrument (piano) patterns in 4/4 time. Meter mismatch handling can be deferred.
The validation_report output is essential for debugging and for building a feedback loop to improve rearrangement quality over time.
Test extensively with ii-V-I progressions in all 12 keys as the baseline regression suite.
Test quality-change rearrangements: take a pattern from a major-key ii-V-I and remap it to a minor-key iiø-V-i to verify the adaptation rules work correctly.
The rearrangement engine should NEVER silently drop notes. Every note in the source pattern must produce a corresponding note in the output, even if flagged with a conflict.
Ghost notes (very low velocity) should be preserved during rearrangement; they contribute to groove feel.
When building the Pattern DB, extract patterns at multiple granularities: 1-bar, 2-bar, 4-bar, and full-phrase. Different retrieval scenarios need different lengths.
The humanize_offset_ticks preservation is what separates a mechanical-sounding output from a natural one. Treat it as a first-class feature, not an afterthought.
Consider storing the analysis engine's confidence scores alongside each pattern's originating_chord_sequence so retrieval can prefer patterns whose source analysis was high-confidence.

downstream.module: MIDI Export / Post-Processing Engine (to be designed)
